section.heading: 6.6. Area Between Two Curves
section.paragraph: Suppose a certain country’s petroleum consumption is expected to be $$f(t)$$ million barrels per year, $$t$$ years from now, for the next $$5$$ years. Then the country’s total petroleum consumption over the period of time in question is given by the area of the region under the graph of $$f$$ on the interval $$\lbrack 0,5\rbrack$$ (Figure 27).

The curve labeled y = g(t) enters the first quadrant from a point in the vertical axis closer to the origin, slopes upward to the right, concave up increasing steeply to the right and exits the first quadrant at the top right of the viewing window. A vertical line is raised from the coordinate (5, 0), which meets the curve. The region below the curve, till the coordinate (5, 0) is shaded.

figure.caption: At a rate of consumption of $$f(t)$$ million barrels per year, the total petroleum consumption is given by the area of the region under the graph of $$f$$ .

section.paragraph: Next, suppose that because of the implementation of certain energy-conservation measures, the petroleum consumption is expected to be $$g(t)$$ million barrels per year instead. Then, the country’s projected total petroleum consumption over the $$5$$ -year period is given by the area of the region under the graph of $$g$$ on the interval $$\lbrack 0,5\rbrack$$ (Figure 28).

image.alt: Details A curve is graphed in a coordinate plane. The horizontal axis t ranges from 0 to over 5 years and the vertical axis y labeled million barrels per year. The curve labeled y = g(t) enters the first quadrant from a point in the vertical axis closer to the origin, slopes upward to the right, concave up increasing gradually to the right and exits the first quadrant on the right of the viewing window. A vertical line is raised from the coordinate (5, 0), which meets the curve. The region below the curve, till the coordinate (5, 0) is shaded.

figure.caption: At a rate of consumption of $$g(t)$$ million barrels per year, the total petroleum consumption is given by the area of the region under the graph of $$g$$ .

section.paragraph: Therefore, the area of the shaded region $$S$$ lying between the graphs of $$f$$ and $$g$$ on the interval $$\lbrack 0,5\rbrack$$ (Figure 29) gives the amount of petroleum that would be saved over the $$5$$ -year period because of the conservation measures.

A vertical line is raised from the coordinate (5, 0), which cuts both the curves. The region between the two curves enclosed by the perpendicular is shaded and labeled S.

section.paragraph: This example shows that some practical problems can be solved by finding the area of a region between two curves, which in turn can be found by evaluating an appropriate definite integral.
section.heading: Finding the Area of the Region Between Two Curves
section.paragraph: We now turn our attention to the general problem of finding the area of a plane region bounded both above and below by the graphs of functions. First, consider the situation in which the graph of one function lies above that of another. More specifically, let $$R$$ be the region in the $$\mathit{xy}$$ -plane (Figure 30) that is bounded above by the graph of a continuous function $$f$$ , below by the graph of a continuous function $$g$$ , where $$f(x) \geq g(x) \geq 0$$ on $$\lbrack a,b\rbrack$$ , and to the left and right by the vertical lines $$x = a$$ and $$x = b$$ , respectively. From the figure, we see that

$$\begin{array}{l} {{Area of}R = { \text{Area of the region under the graph of} f(x) - {Area of the region under the graph of}g(x)}} \\ {\phantom{{Area of}R} = {\int_{a}^{b}{f(x)\mathit{dx} - {\int_{a}^{b}{g(x)\mathit{dx}}}}}} \\ {\phantom{{Area of}R} = {\int_{a}^{b}{\left\lbrack f(x) - g(x) \right\rbrack\mathit{dx}}}} \end{array}$$

example.paragraph: Find the area of the region bounded by the $$x$$ -axis, the graph of $$y = - x^{2} + 4x - 8$$ , and the lines $$x = - 1$$ and $$x = 4$$ .
example.heading: Solution
example.paragraph: The region $$R$$ under consideration is shown in Figure 31. We can view $$R$$ as the region bounded above by the graph of $$f(x) = 0$$ (the $$x$$ -axis) and below by the graph of $$g{(x)} = - x^{2} + 4x - 8$$ on $$\lbrack - 1,4\rbrack$$ . Therefore, the area of $$R$$ is given by

$$\begin{array}{l} {{\int_{a}^{b}{\lbrack f(x) - g(x)\rbrack\mathit{dx}}} = {\int_{- 1}^{4}{\lbrack{0 - {({- x^{2} + 4x - 8})}\rbrack}\mathit{dx}}}} \\ {\phantom{\int_{a}^{b}{\left\lbrack f(x) - g(x) \right\rbrack\mathit{dx}}} = {\int_{- 1}^{4}{({x^{2} - 4x + 8})}\mathit{dx}}} \\ {\phantom{\int_{a}^{b}{\left\lbrack f(x) - g(x) \right\rbrack\mathit{dx}}} = \left. \frac{1}{3}x^{3} - 2x^{2} + 8x \right|_{- 1}^{4}} \\ {\phantom{\int_{a}^{b}{\left\lbrack f(x) - g(x) \right\rbrack\mathit{dx}}} = \left\lbrack {\frac{1}{3}{(64)} - 2{(16)} + 8{(4)}} \right\rbrack - \left\lbrack {\frac{1}{3}{({- 1})} - 2{(1)} + 8{({- 1})}} \right\rbrack} \\ {\phantom{\int_{a}^{b}{\left\lbrack f(x) - g(x) \right\rbrack\mathit{dx}}} = {31\frac{2}{3}}} \end{array}$$

$$\begin{array}{l} {{\int_{0}^{5}\left\lbrack {R_{1}(t) - R(t)} \right\rbrack\mathit{dt}} = {\int_{0}^{5}{({20e^{0.08t} - 20e^{0.05t}})}\mathit{dt}}} \\ {\phantom{\int_{0}^{5}\left\lbrack {R_{1}(t) - R(t)} \right\rbrack\mathit{dt}} = {20{\int_{0}^{5}{({e^{0.08t} - e^{0.05t}})}\mathit{dt}}}} \\ {\phantom{\int_{0}^{5}\left\lbrack {R_{1}(t) - R(t)} \right\rbrack\mathit{dt}} = \left. 20\left( {\frac{e^{0.08t}}{0.08} - \frac{e^{0.05t}}{0.05}} \right) \right|_{0}^{5}} \\ {\phantom{\int_{0}^{5}\left\lbrack {R_{1}(t) - R(t)} \right\rbrack\mathit{dt}} = \left. 20\left\lbrack \left( {\frac{e^{0.4}}{0.08} - \frac{e^{0.25}}{0.05}} \right) - \left( {\frac{1}{0.08} - \frac{1}{0.05}} \right) \right. \right\rbrack} \\ {\phantom{\int_{0}^{5}\left\lbrack {R_{1}(t) - R(t)} \right\rbrack\mathit{dt}} \approx 9.3} \end{array}$$

section.heading: Using Technology -- Finding the Area Between Two Curves
section.paragraph: The numerical integral operation can be used to find the area between two curves. We do this by using the numerical integral operation to evaluate an appropriate definite integral or the sum (difference) of appropriate definite integrals. In the following example, the intersection operation is also used to advantage to help us find the limits of integration.
